I'm impressed by (and worried about) AI models in many respects. I use them all the time, they're good at a lot of things and superhuman at some. Their lack of creativity is noteworthy though. And also shows up in more technical problems (rarely have "A-ha!" moments).

I think it's actually kind of revealing how shitty this is it's just random incoherent tropes

Trying a different version of this chart. Basically, South America is underrated (by FIFA and tbh in most other respects).

This is actually part of the issue with the FIFA rankings. The USA plays a *lot* of home matches, and FIFA doesn't even account for home field! So that biases our rating upwards except when games are actually played at home, which fortunately, they are just this once.

Well, at least you can't accuse me of playing favorites for our subscriber list (78% American).

FIFA's ranking for the US probably isn't right, I *will* say though that we tend to find a bigger home-field advantage than other models. MEX has a particularly big one.


Eli Dourado (@elidourado)

FIFA has USA at #16, PELE has USA at #37. Seems right, sadly.

How popular is Donald Trump?. Silver Bulletin approval ratings for President Trump — and all presidents since Truman.
How popular is the Iran War? . Silver Bulletin approval ratings for the ongoing conflict.
Who’s ahead on the generic congressional ballot?. Our constantly-updating tracker of polls for the most important indicator in the race for Congress.
On redistricting, Democrats are playing as the away team. Democrats are fighting uphill against Republican-leaning courts. But they can’t afford either despondence or complacency.
How we calculate our PELE ratings. Way more detail than you asked for on the methods behind our new soccer model.

Want more Black representatives? Elect more Democrats.. I ran the numbers on redistricting after the Supreme Court's decision on the Voting Rights Act. The Black representation trade-off is mostly a myth.
Democrats are not OK with Boomers. Perhaps having learned their lesson with Joe Biden, the party’s voters are starting to reject older, establishment-bound candidates.
How much can Trump screw with the midterms? (by Eli McKown-Dawson). Doomsday scenarios are unlikely, but the realistic ones deserve more attention. A Q&A with Votebeat's Nathaniel Rakich.
How popular is Elon Musk? . Silver Bulletin favorability ratings for the world's richest man.
Can we please stop rationalizing political violence?
Yes, Virginia, redistricting is a two-player game. Democratic voters are pretty rational. For once, their leadership has been, too.
SBSQ #31: Trump is super unpopular. So why don’t Democrats have a bigger lead?. A deeper look at the generic ballot. Plus, the game theory of the automated strike zone. And more models coming soon!
The profoundly weird race for Rookie of the Year (by Joseph George). Dramatic late twists, stats versus vibes — and another test of what prediction markets really measure.
"Engagement" is a dumb metric. An algorithm doesn’t always tell you what content people truly find valuable. Plus more from my chat with Mike Solana.
